sections.text:
In a small, old hut on the outskirts of the village, a boy named Jake lived with his poor widowed mother.

They did not own anything in the world except a dairy cow called “White,” whose only source of livelihood was selling its milk.

But one day, the cow stopped producing milk, so they had nothing to eat.

The mother said sadly: “Jake, you must go to the village market tomorrow and sell our dear cow so we can buy food for it.”

The next morning, Jake set off with the cow to market, and halfway there, he met an eccentric old man.

The old man looked at the cow and said, "That's a beautiful cow, Jake! How about you give it to me for these five beans?"

Jake laughed and said, "Five beans for a whole cow? That's crazy!"

The old man said in a low, confidential voice: “These are not ordinary beans, my son. They are magic beans! If you plant them at night, they will grow and reach the sky the next morning!”

Naive Jake was fascinated by the idea, agreed to the exchange, and returned home happy.

When his mother saw the beans and heard the story, she became very angry and cried bitterly because she lost her only cow.

She took the beans and threw them out the window angrily, sending Jake to bed without food as punishment.

Jake fell asleep feeling guilty, but when he woke up the next morning, he noticed his room was dark.

He looked out the window, and was shocked by what he saw! The beans have grown and formed a very giant green tree, whose upper trunk disappears between the clouds in the sky!
Jake remembered the old man's words, and without telling his mother, he began climbing the sturdy bean stalk up toward the sky.

He climbed and climbed for long hours, until he finally reached the clouds, and there he found a wide stone path leading to a very huge and terrifying castle.

Jake entered the castle briskly, and hid behind a huge door when he heard heavy footsteps shaking the ground: Boom! Boom! Boom!
This was the voice of a huge, terrifying giant. He entered the room, sniffing the air and saying in his thundering voice: “I smell a human being! Whether alive or dead, I will grind him to make my bread!”

Jake hid in the oven, shivering, while the giant sat down and took out a bag full of gold coins and began counting them until he fell asleep and began to snore.

Jake crept out quietly, took the bag of gold, and hurried down the beanstalk to his house.

His mother was happy with the gold and they lived comfortably for a while, but when the gold ran out, Jake decided to climb the tree again.

This time, Jake hid and saw the giant bringing a strange chicken, and commanded it: “My eggs!”, and the chicken laid an egg of pure gold!
When the giant fell asleep, Jake stole the wondrous chicken and returned it to his mother, and they became rich and no longer needed money.

But Jake's curiosity pushed him to go up a third and final time, and this time he saw the giant playing a magical golden harp that played the most beautiful melodies and sang itself!
When the giant fell asleep, Jake grabbed the harp to escape with it, but the magic harp screamed loudly: “Master! Oh master! They are stealing from me!”

The giant woke up angry and saw Jake running, so he started chasing him with his huge steps that almost crushed Jake.

Jake reached the beanstalk and began descending as fast as he could, the giant descending behind him.

"Mom! Mom! Get the ax quick!" shouted Jake as he approached the ground.

The mother ran and gave him the axe, and Jake began hitting the huge tree trunk with all his might until it broke.

The great tree fell to the ground, and the evil giant fell with it and died instantly.

Jake and his mother lived in wealth and happiness thanks to the hen that lays golden eggs, and Jake learned that courage does not mean excessive greed.
